name: Nuala
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nuala was one of the children of Lir. She and her four brothers could still speak like people even though their bodies had become swans. Decca demanded to see the swan-children. Her husband refused, and she left him. He then yielded and ordered the swans carried to the palace. There Decca watched them turn back into people. At once they died of old age and turned to dust before her eyes.
